sentences.text:
Bench: Sanjay Kishan Kaul, Sudhanshu Dhulia
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Original Jurisdiction
 Transfer Petition(s)(Civil) No(s). 
 Monica Preeti Joseph 
 Versus
 Vanraj Naidu 
 with
 T.P.(Crl.) No. 211/2023
 O R D E R
The marriage between the parties was solemnized as per Christian rites and customs on 07.4.2021.
It is stated that the marriage was through a matrimonial website.
There are no issues out of the wedlock.
On 16.2.2023, with joint request of parties the matter was referred to the Supreme Court Mediation Centre.
The mediation report has been received enclosing the settlement agreement dated 19.5.2023.

It is stated in the settlement agreement that both the parties lived at Bangalore from April, 2021 till January 2022 but on account of difference in temperaments, there have been litigation since then.
The usual bouquet of cases in the form of five litigations as enumerated in the settlement agreement Reason: have arisen.
Both the parties have agreed to settle the matrimonial dispute.
It is stated that the parties had a joint locker in Bangalore and the petitioner has already taken back all her goods and the locker has been closed.

A sum of Rs.15,00,000/- has been agreed to be paid towards full and final settlement of all claims whatsoever of the petitioner which were agreed to be paid by the respondent on 19.5.2023 and 26.6.2023.
These amounts are stated to be paid.
Learned counsel for the parties have produced before us the affidavits filed by the parties.
This is so as it appears that the page Nos.3 & 4 of the settlement agreement are not on record and the Mediation Centre should be called to send the said pages to complete the settlement agreement.
The jurisdiction of this Court under Article 142 of the Constitution of India is invoked and divorce is also sought by mutual consent under Section 28 of the Special Marriage Act, 1954.

sentences.text: Christian, the mutual divorce is permissible under Section 10A of the Indian Divorce Act,1869.
Petitioner is present in the Court and respondent is connected virtually.

In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances and looking to the provisions of the divorce under the aforesaid two Acts as also by exercising jurisdiction under Article 142 of the Constitution of India we are of the view that mutual consent divorce is liable to T.P.(C) No. 1822/2022 & T.P (Crl.)
No. 211/2023 2 be granted inter se the parties on terms and conditions of the settlement agreement.
The parties will abide by the terms of the settlement.
The monetary compensation in full and final settlement has already been paid.
In view of the agreement, all the proceedings inter se the parties are closed/ quashed as enumerated therein entisted below:

(i) Divorce Case- M.C. No.1954 of 2022 titled as Vanraj Naidu V. Monica Preeti Joseph pending before Principal Judge, Family Court, Bangalore.
(ii) Maintenance Case- Criminal Misc. Application No.382 of 2022 titled Monica Preeti Joseph Vs. Vanraj Naidu; pending before the Principal Judge, Family Court,
Rampur.
(iii) FIR No.282 of 2022 registered under Sections 498A, 323, 354, 376, 511 IPC R/w sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, pending before the Civil Lines Police Station, Rampur.
